paper_sections.title: ICA: effects of Task, Language and Age
Role of GMD in mediating age-related overactivation
Performing an explicit task versus listening to sentences

description.value: The study examined age-related modulation of language-processing networks during explicit sentence acceptability judgments versus natural listening, using task-based group ICA of fMRI and mediation analysis of grey matter density.

spans.text: Here we test this hypothesis in adults aged 20–86 years by combining measures of language comprehension, functional connectivity and neural integrity to identify functional networks activated in two language experiments with varying task demands.

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional study of 50 healthy adults aged 20–86 years, evenly divided between task and natural-listening experiments; the participant pools did not overlap.

spans.text: The participants consisted of 50 healthy, native British English speakers across a broad range of ages (20–86 years).
There was no overlap in the participant pools between the   task   and   natural listening   experiments.
MNI coordinates for significant mediation clusters.

definition.value: Voxel-wise mediation of the age-related increase in bilateral PFC ICA network expression by grey matter density, identifying clusters showing the conjunction of age-related decline in GMD, the relationship between GMD and ICA loading, and attenuation of the age–ICA relationship.

spans.text: We restrict our results to clusters demonstrating a significant effect (  p  <0.01, 15 contiguous voxels) across all paths in the model (conjunction of   a  ,   b  , and   ab   effects).
Voxel-wise mediation was performed using the M-MEPM toolbox ( Wager et al. 2009 ).

within: 1) the age-related decline in GMD (the   a   effect), 2) the relationship between GMD and ICA loading on the bilateral PFC network, controlling for age (the   b   effect) and 3) the extent to which the GMD in a given voxel explains a significant amount of the age-ICA covariance (  ab   effect).
